summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 27.9% to INR642.3 crores and PAT to INR174.3 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 34.6% and working capital days rose to 213.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew 27.9% YoY to INR642.3 crores, with EBITDA up 16.8% to INR221.9 crores and PAT up to INR174.3 crores from INR138.7 crores. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 15.7% to INR182.3 crores, with EBITDA of INR62.6 crores at a 34.3% margin. Specialty ingredients grew 62% to INR280 crores and rose to 44% of revenue, while pharma, food and nutrition grew 10%. Working capital days increased from 184 to 213 on higher raw material and finished goods inventory, and management targets 150-160 days within FY27.

segments.name: Pharma, food and nutrition
segments.commentary: About 56% of FY26 revenue, growing 10% YoY on calcium and iron demand; management cites volume growth above 20%, with the phosphate price increase only passed through from Q1 FY27. Utilisation is 65-70%.

segments.name: Specialty ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from INR172 crores to INR280 crores (+62%), share of revenue rose from 34% to about 44%. Utilisation is 35-40%. Growth drivers are encapsulation and premix approvals.

segments.name: Sudeep Advanced Materials (battery materials)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 of 25,000 MT per year targeted for commissioning by April 2027 at Dahej. Around 5,000-7,000 MT of battery-grade iron phosphate can be made in the existing pharma facility; about 700 MT of initial POs received in the last month.

segments.name: NSS (Ireland, nutrition blending)
segments.commentary: Acquired May 2025; integration is progressing. New business head Mattias Fredrickson appointed to drive expansion outside Ireland, especially in Europe infant nutrition and critical care.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give direct revenue guidance but expects pharma, food and nutrition growth in FY27 to exceed the 10% of FY26, and specialty ingredients to track its recent 2-3 year growth.
Consolidated EBITDA and PAT margins expected to recover over the next couple of quarters toward FY24-FY25 levels; analyst's question on 37-38% margin in FY27 was confirmed as correct by management.
Pharma, food and nutrition EBITDA expected to grow about 15% in FY27 and FY28, as hiring costs are already in the base.
FY27 capex: about INR10 crores to complete the greenfield project and about INR15 crores maintenance capex, excluding SAM capex.
Management expects around 2,500 MT of battery material sales in FY27, confirmed as a fair assumption.
Non-battery business could scale to INR1,000-1,200 crores with the commissioned greenfield facility and no incremental capex.
Working capital days targeted to fall to 150-160 days within FY27.
capex_capacity: Gross capex in FY26 was INR127 crores: INR34 crores for SAM land, INR80 crores for the greenfield project, and INR13 crores maintenance.

Greenfield facility completed internal production validation and qualification; customer qualification takes 6-12 months. It will add glycinate and gluconate capacity. Commissioning was delayed by LPG and energy shortages.
Battery materials Phase 1 (25,000 MT per year) at Dahej targeted for April 2027. Groundbreaking done in FY26.

Total battery materials capex for 100,000 MT is about INR600 crores, including land and Phase 2 infrastructure. Revenue potential at 100,000 MT is INR1,600-1,800 crores at about $2/kg average price (as stated).
Current utilisation: pharma, food and nutrition 65-70%; specialty ingredients 35-40%.
demand_pricing: Phosphoric acid cost spike from higher global sulfur costs; management says the price impact was passed to customers without material margin compression, with the phosphate price increase effective from Q1 FY27.

Bisglycinate (AbsorBis brand) has approvals from two large US consumers; the global market is about $1 billion, with North America 40-50% of demand. Management said realisation is about 4x the current portfolio.

Battery materials: 42 customers in qualification (22 lab, 14 pilot, 6 commercial validation in off-take talks) across Korea, Japan, Indonesia, India, Europe and the US. Management says the goal is ex-China supply, not competing on price with China.
About 51 new customer approvals in FY26 versus FY25. Specialty ingredients growth tied to encapsulation (largest global bakery plus two of the top five) and premix (a large infant nutrition company).

qa_highlights.question: Why is pharma, food and nutrition EBITDA growing slower than volume, and what is the FY27-28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth exceeded 20% with a mix shift; the phosphate price pass-through started in Q1. Margin was diluted by glycinate and gluconate running on a small temporary line, and by hiring for the greenfield plant. Management expects about 15% EBITDA growth in FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about INR3 crores CSR spend, about INR1.5 crores of LPG premium costs in March, and about INR2 crores of air freight to the largest customer. These are expected to fall in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much battery material volume is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is commercially making battery-grade iron phosphate in the existing pharma facility (5,000-7,000 MT capacity), with about half for commercial orders. It agreed that about 2,500 MT of sales in FY27 is a fair assumption.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and revenue economics for battery materials?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR600 crores covers 100,000 MT including land and Phase 2 infrastructure, so it is not INR300 crores per 25,000 MT. Revenue potential at full capacity is INR1,600-1,800 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-battery revenue potential and margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Without incremental capex, the existing portfolio can scale to INR1,000-1,200 crores. Margin should recover toward the historical 24-25% (per the management answer), and bisglycinate should add higher-margin revenue from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How do realisations and competition compare for new molecules?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify margins or a realisation premium for battery materials and new molecules, citing confidentiality. It did say bisglycinate realisation is about four times the current portfolio, and that competition is mainly with a US market leader on performance rather than price.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on phosphoric acid and LPG pricing, and on the pass-through timing (Q1-Q2 FY27).
Working capital at 213 days needs to fall to 150-160 days; inventory of INR88 crores added in FY26 (raw material +INR41 crores to INR95 crores; finished goods +INR37 crores) must liquidate.
Greenfield commissioning was delayed by LPG and energy shortages; customer qualification of 6-12 months could delay volume ramp.
Battery materials Phase 1 targeted for April 2027; the 700 MT PO flow and conversion of 6 customers in off-take talks are unproven. Management did not disclose battery margins.
Management declined to disclose margin and realisation detail for new molecules and battery materials, limiting analyst visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and pipeline, but cautious and somewhat evasive on margin, realisation and battery unit economics, which management declined to quantify. Management acknowledged FY26 margin pressure and attributed it to temporary factors.
key_quotes: We expect customer qualification timelines to range between six to 12 months, depending on product categories and customer audit requirements.

Encouragingly, we have also started receiving initial commercial purchase orders, including approximately 700 metric tons over the last month alone, supporting customer efforts to diversify sourcing away from China.
